NHPC Ltd. Citing it as supportive, refining authority is backwards.

note: Celir LLP v Bafna Motors (21 Sept 2023, right to redeem extinguished on publication of auction notice, not on sale completion) is correctly stated and well corroborated; Mathew Varghese is correctly described as the pre-amendment position. However, the guide's own verification_notes incorrectly asserts that no 2024-2026 decision applying or refining Celir LLP could be found. In fact the Supreme Court decided M. Rajendran and Ors. v. KPK Oils and Proteins India Pvt. Ltd. on 22 September 2025 (Pardiwala and Mahadevan JJ.), expressly reaffirming Celir LLP and clarifying that 'publication' means the composite notice process (service, newspaper publication, affixation and website upload). This on-point, confirming Supreme Court decision should be reflected rather than omitted as nonexistent.

fixes.find: Where an auction notice has already been published and the borrower missed that window, Celir LLP leaves very little room to argue the point before the DRT or a civil court based on the SARFAESI provision itself.
fixes.replace: The Supreme Court reaffirmed this position in M. Rajendran and Ors. v. KPK Oils and Proteins India Pvt. Ltd. (decided 22 September 2025), holding again that the redemption right is lost on valid publication of the auction notice and does not survive until confirmation or registration of the sale, and clarifying that 'publication' refers to the composite notice process (service, newspaper publication, affixation and website upload), not a newspaper advertisement alone. Where an auction notice has already been published and the borrower missed that window, this line of authority leaves very little room to argue the point before the DRT or a civil court based on the SARFAESI provision itself.
fixes.reason: Adds the on-point 2025 Supreme Court decision reaffirming Celir LLP, which exists and was missed.
